filename: Reliable coarse-grained turbulent simulations through combined offline learning and neural emulation.pdf
title: Reliable coarse-grained turbulent simulations through combined offline learning and neural emulation
venue: 1st workshop on Synergy of Scientific and Machine Learning Modeling, SynS & ML ICML 2023
parameterization_target: Subgrid potential vorticity forcing (eddy flux divergence)
code_availability: pyqg code cited as publicly available at https://zenodo.org/record/6563667; ML parameterization and emulation code availability is not stated.
testbed_rationale: The paper uses an idealized 2-layer quasi-geostrophic setup generated via pyqg (18,000 snapshots), but does not provide direct public access links or repository locations for the generated dataset.
pain_points: Instabilities and energy accumulation at the gridscale when offline-trained ML parameterizations are coupled online
Inability to differentiate through legacy numerical ocean and climate models to do end-to-end online training
Trade-off between capturing inverse energy cascade/backscatter and ensuring numerical stability
extraction_notes: The paper introduces a loss term with a neural emulator that predicts residuals (q_{i+\Delta t} - q_i) to regularize offline parameterization training toward stable trajectories without needing a differentiable host model.
